title: Release readiness audit and publication preflight
summary: Audited release-readiness surfaces and realigned Tauri publication metadata to the Phase 1 semver identity while preserving the backend calendar release label.
reason: Publication preparation found Tauri package metadata carrying a dirty 0.0.0 build identity even though the active release-foundation plan requires semver-compatible 6.0.0 Tauri metadata for the 2026.06.04.001 portable release.
behavior_before: The backend release label remained 2026.06.04.001, but Tauri package.json, package-lock.json, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, and tauri.conf.json used 0.0.0 or a dirty build suffix inconsistent with Phase 1 publication identity.
behavior_after: Tauri package, npm lock, Cargo manifest, Cargo lock, and Tauri config all report semver 6.0.0; backend release label/product-version metadata remains 2026.06.04.001.
manual_validation: rg stale 0.0.0 Tauri identity scan: no matches in active Tauri/release-foundation/test surfaces
pytest focused Tauri identity/versioning tests: 5 passed
apps/desktop/tauri/Test-TauriShell-Build.ps1: passed; cargo check/test/build reported mediapipeline-tauri-shell v6.0.0 and 38 Rust tests passed
ops/scripts/release/build.ps1 -DryRun: passed; no files copied; default plan strips live config, runtime state, logs, node modules, Tauri target output, and tests

ops/scripts/release/test.ps1 -SkipToolIntegration -SkipEndToEndSmoke: passed after regenerating generated project maps; source/dev manifest hygiene, tool integration, and end-to-end media smoke remained intentionally skipped/downshifted
rollback_plan: Revert only the Tauri semver metadata, Phase 4 candidate-name doc edits, static test addition, generated summary, and this packet. No media files, source/scratch/output paths, pending publish manifests, queue state, settings persistence, or FFmpeg/audio/subtitle policy are touched.
notes: Release-readiness audit also found publication is still blocked by the pre-existing dirty worktree and in-progress network/config/WebView changes outside this packet. Public/manual publication still requires operator approval plus Phase 4 candidate build, Phase 5 package open/close validation, Phase 6 real-media pilot evidence for the same candidate, signing/unsigned-distribution decision confirmation, license/third-party/privacy/security notices, finalized release notes, and strict change-control coverage.
